subject: Rivermark pilot: request for non‑standard latency remedy & discount
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@rivermark.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot SLA ask: temporary latency guardrail and credit scheme

Hi Marissa / Ben,

Thanks again for running the pilot with us. We completed the initial throughput runs last week and have a couple of product constraints that mean we’ll see a higher 95th‑percentile latency than originally estimated for the first 30 days of production (heavy multimodal inference during onboarding).

To keep the pilot moving we’d like Redwood to accept a temporary latency guardrail: P95 <= 200ms for the first 30 days (instead of the standard 100ms target), and a remedial approach that prioritizes a one‑time onboarding credit rather than continuous per‑minute service credits. Specifically: a one‑time 10% credit on month‑one bill if observed P95 > 200ms but < 300ms; if P95 exceeds 300ms we accept standard service credits but would like a cap on total credits during the pilot.

We know this is non‑standard so please route to your deal desk / execs. We’re also asking for a 15% pilot discount on the committed capacity in exchange for the relaxed latency target.

Attached: short note with measurements and our suggested MAP.

Sanjay Rao
Director of Platform Engineering, Rivermark Systems
attachments: Rivermark_Pilot_Run_Summary.csv (csv)
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA ask: temporary latency guardrail and credit scheme

Marissa / Avery / Lauren — looping you in.

Quick summary: Rivermark wants a temporary P95 latency guardrail of 200ms for 30 days and a one‑time onboarding credit (10% of month‑one invoice) as the primary remediation for small regressions. They also asked for a 15% pilot discount. If P95 > 300ms they want standard service credits but with a pilot cap.

Their pilot looks strategic (pilot -> paid expansion with multiple teams). I recommend we offer a structured carveout:
- One‑time onboarding credit (10%) for 200ms < P95 <= 300ms
- Standard service credits for P95 > 300ms but limited by a pilot cap (recommend $50k)
- Pilot discount: 10% (rather than 15%) — can escalate to exec for the extra 5% if necessary

MAP attached (draft). If Deal Desk & Legal are fine with the cap and wording, we should get an exec signoff for the extra 5% discount and the $50k cap.

— Ben

Subject: Fwd: Pilot SLA ask — Deal Desk recommendation and redline

Marissa — forwarding the redline and Deal Desk recommendation. See attachments: Rivermark_SLA_Redline_v3.pdf (pdf), MAP_Rivermark_Pilot.xlsx (xlsx), Deal_Summary_RIV-2027-091.pdf (pdf).

Deal Desk recommended terms (summary for exec):
- Pilot term: 60 days (30 day active pilot + 30 day observation).
- Latency guardrail (temporary): P95 <= 200ms for pilot active window. Normal target (100ms) to resume after observation window.
- Remediation: one‑time onboarding credit equal to 10% of month‑one invoice if observed P95 in (200ms, 300ms].
- If P95 > 300ms: apply standard service credits per SLA but limit cumulative credits for pilot to $50,000.
- Pilot discount: 10% off committed capacity for first billing period.
- No make‑whole / indemnity language. Legal asks to avoid open ended ‘make‑whole’ language and to keep remedies capped.

Request: executive approval to grant the additional 5% discount (to meet customer ask of 15%) and approval to finalize the $50k pilot credit cap. If exec approves the extra 5% we’ll finalize with Legal and circulate the redline to Rivermark.

Avery Johnson
Deal Desk Lead — Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot SLA ask — Deal Desk recommendation and redline

Thanks for the clear summary and for keeping the legal constraints in mind. A few clarifying Qs before I sign off:
1) Is the $50k cap inclusive of the one‑time 10% onboarding credit or is that separate? (I’d prefer inclusive so total downside is fixed.)
2) Can Legal express an explicit transition clause that returns the customer to standard SLA targets after the observation window, and prevents retroactive claims beyond the pilot window?
3) For the extra 5% discount request: what’s the revenue tradeoff vs. the expansion probability you’re modeling? I want to make sure the incremental discount is justified by expected expansion.

If answers are acceptable I’m prepared to approve the extra 5% discount (bringing pilot discount to 15%) and to commit to the $50k total cap (inclusive). Approvals should be conditioned on Legal adding the transition language and Sales documenting the MAP milestones.

— Marissa
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 28 Jul 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: APPROVED: Rivermark pilot non‑standard terms (conditions)

Sanjay / Priya — thanks for the patience and for outlining the MAP. I’ve reviewed Deal Desk’s recommendation and will approve the non‑standard terms on the following conditions (final):

1) Pilot discount: 15% off committed capacity for first billing period (approved).
2) Remediation: one‑time onboarding credit equal to 10% of month‑one invoice if observed P95 is >200ms and <=300ms.
3) If P95 >300ms, standard SLA service credits apply but total credits/monetary remediation for the pilot cannot exceed $50,000 (this cap is inclusive of the onboarding credit).
4) The pilot term will be 60 days (30d active + 30d observation). At the end of the observation window the SLA targets revert to standard thresholds; no retroactive claims beyond the pilot observation period. Legal will finalize the transition clause.
5) Sales & Customer Success will execute the attached MAP (Milestones & acceptance criteria) and provide daily ops runbooks during the first 14 days.

Please confirm acceptance of these terms and I’ll instruct Legal to issue the redline and a DocuSign for signatures. Once signed, we’ll apply the 15% discount on the first invoice and record the $50k cap in our deal system (Deal ID RIV-2027-091).

Best —
Marissa Cole
VP, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
